# Further lane-exact schedules for 112 and 160 bowlers

Both schedules have groups of four, every pair meets once, every player visits each lane pair once or twice, and playing positions are balanced. Player IDs start at 1.

## Construction

Take four copies of a base roster of size m. Use a six-column orthogonal array of strength two and order m. Its first two columns specify a week and lane. The other four select one player from each roster copy. These m weeks cover all pairs between copies, and each player visits every lane once.

To cover pairs inside each copy, draw the base schedule in four copies side by side. For each original lane, colour its groups with four colours so that groups sharing a player receive different colours. A group of colour c from copy h goes to the corresponding original lane in quarter (h+c) modulo four. Every week fills every lane once. Each player visits any lane at most once in this internal phase, giving one or two visits overall.

The 28-player base admits such a colouring, as does the 40-player base. For order 28 the array uses a difference matrix on the additive group of order 28 from the Handbook of Combinatorial Designs. For order 40 it is the direct product of the finite-field constructions of orders five and eight.

This construction can be iterated. Every output lane has two disjoint-block families, one from each phase, so the required colouring is available again. For later orders in the two families use the direct product of a power-of-two field with the field of order seven or five. Thus all roster sizes 28 × 4^j and 40 × 4^j exist for every integer j ≥ 0.

[SageMath difference-matrix source, DM_28_6_1](https://github.com/sagemath/sage/blob/develop/src/sage/combinat/designs/database.py)
